A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same occupation-generation study and retain identifiable methods, experiments, and results. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original persona and biography generation experiments with three LLMs, including gender distributions, gender-association validation, significant word differences, and representational-bias scores.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation experiments and reports additional calibration sensitivity, clustering, uncertainty estimates, and between-model significance tests.

M1.justification: The probing stage changes from manually constructed word categories to K-means++ clustering in Section 5.3. The core gender-association, calibrated-word, and SRB-score procedures remain. Naming the pipeline GAS(P) and identifying the existing similarity calculation as Chamfer distance do not themselves change those procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions study the same 63 occupations, persona and biography prompts, and explicitly prompted versus unprompted gender representation. Female, male, and non-binary representation remain covered, with detailed representational comparisons restricted to women and men. The added analyses introduce no new task or population.

E2.justification: The comparison against Cheng et al.'s Marked Personas remains in v1 Tables 3–4 and v2 Tables 7–8. The three studied LLMs and BLS reference also remain. GenBiT and WEAT receive additional conceptual discussion in v2, but are not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported calibration mixture changes from p=0.25 in v1 Appendix B.2 to alpha=0.15 selected through a 0–1 search in 0.05 increments in v2 Appendix A.2. The replacement clustering analysis introduces M3 embeddings, 1500 clusters, preprocessing, and prevalence thresholds. These substantially revise the analysis protocol; generation prompts, budgets, and the 10% eligibility rule remain.

E4.justification: v1's manually categorized stereotype analyses and category-count plots are replaced by cluster-based analysis of gendered word prevalence in v2 Figure 5. v2 also adds prior-mixture sensitivity results in Tables 3 and 5 and a silhouette analysis of cluster-number selection in Figure 8.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports Bernoulli standard errors for occupation-level female representation in Table 11 and between-model SRB significance tests in Table 14. v1 already reports word-level significance and within-model Welch tests. Neither version establishes additional independent repetitions or a new seed-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Representation plots, calibrated word lists, and SRB statistics change. For example, GPT-3.5's Welch statistic changes from -11.54 to -11.79, with p changing from approximately 3.1391e-16 to 1.4410e-16. New results include 1346 of 1500 clusters exhibiting gender-skewed prevalence and per-model software-engineer word lists. Manual-category results are removed. Revised calibration prevents interpreting these updates as same-setting model improvements.

T1.justification: v1's Subset Similarity Metric and v2's cosine-based Chamfer distance express the same average nearest-neighbor distance; the SRB difference formula is retained. The versions add no substantive theorem, proof, or new mathematical property. The additional metric explanations and examples are expository.

C1.justification: The central finding that increased female representation coexists with gendered representational harms remains. v2 explicitly presents GAS(P) as a general evaluation framework and identifies the underlying distance as Chamfer distance. Its conclusion also makes proliferation conditional on increasing representation without addressing harms, softening v1's more direct proliferation claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit markedness and passion-related interpretations and limitations concerning U.S. labor data, classification errors, computational demands, and cluster selection. Extended interpretations concerning appearance, environmental stereotypes, mental health, and resilience are removed rather than merely relocated. v1's warnings against metric gaming and its discussion of difficulties extending gender association to other demographics are also omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds the exact Llama endpoint, TogetherAI usage, user-role prompting, validation-set composition, explicit significance threshold, and clustering implementation and filtering details. Much foundational reproducibility information—prompts, generation budgets, pseudocode, GPT snapshot identifiers, and the code/data repository—was already provided in v1.

R1.justification: Research positioning is substantially revised around unprompted group-bias measurement in generated text. v2 distinguishes its contribution from image-bias analysis, Swinger et al.'s embedding analysis, GenBiT, and WEAT, and adds related hiring-bias research. It also removes extensive social-science references supporting the discarded appearance, resilience, and other stereotype discussions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, methodology, and discussion are extensively rewritten around GAS(P). Methodological subsections are regrouped, implications and conclusion are merged, substantial discussion moves into reorganized appendices, and a checklist and appendix contents page are added. This exceeds terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds a pipeline diagram, replaces the two category-based bar-chart figures with a cluster-prevalence display, and adds a silhouette plot and sensitivity, uncertainty, example-generation, and word-list tables. Existing SRB heatmaps reorder occupations and distinguish missing entries with gray cells. The document also adopts a different publication layout.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the analysis more inspectable through systematic clustering, calibration sensitivity results, fuller examples, clearer positioning, and explicit limitations. These improve transparency beyond v1's manually selected categories. The gain is limited by unresolved reporting issues: Section 5.3 and Appendix C.3.1 give unexplained selected-cluster totals of 30 and 86, and Table 11's standard errors below 0.003 are not reconciled with the stated 100 generations per prompt.
